{
  "research_question": "Does stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) significantly affect mouse navigation performance metrics?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Perform a one-way ANOVA for each of the five response variables with 'Stim Paradigm' as the independent factor.",
    "Test H0: mu_Combined = mu_ICMS = mu_DimVisual = mu_BrightVisual = mu_Sham against H1: at least one mean differs.",
    "Order response variables by checking normality and homogeneity of variance violations before selecting the specific ANOVA variant (Standard vs. Welch vs. Robust)."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Normality: Check residuals for each model using Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests; note that 'Success' is binary (0/1) and likely violates normality, requiring a Generalized Linear Model (GLM) with Binomial distribution instead of ANOVA.",
    "Homogeneity of Variance: Levene's test required; 'Success' exhibits extreme heteroscedasticity due to binary nature, while 'Time-to-Target' and 'Path Efficiency' show wide ranges (min=0.5, max=201.39 and min=0.0009, max=29.81 respectively) suggesting potential variance instability.",
    "Independence: Verify that multiple trials per Mouse (8 levels) are independent or account for nested structure (Mouse within Paradigm) using a Mixed Effects Model if residuals show autocorrelation by subject.",
    "Outliers: Inspect 'Time-to-Target' (max=201.39 vs mean=2.80) and 'Path Efficiency' (max=29.81 vs mean=0.47) for extreme values impacting ANOVA robustness."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If any omnibus F-test is significant (p < 0.05) for non-binary variables, proceed with pairwise comparisons.",
    "Apply Tukey's HSD correction for multiple comparisons to control Family-Wise Error Rate.",
    "For 'Success', use a Chi-square test of independence or post-hoc contrasts from the GLM (e.g., pairwise comparisons of proportions with arcsine transformation or logistic regression contrasts).",
    "Report effect sizes (eta-squared for ANOVA, Cohen's h for proportions) alongside p-values."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham group shows substantially lower Success rate (0.27) and higher Time-to-Target (4.68) compared to all other groups, suggesting the Sham condition impairs performance relative to active stimulation.",
    "Sham group shows lower Path Efficiency (0.31) and AD (0.24), indicating less efficient and potentially more dispersed (or less corrected) paths compared to ICMS/Visual groups.",
    "ICMS Only and Visual Only groups show intermediate performance, lower than Combined but higher than Sham, suggesting additive or synergistic effects of stimulation modalities.",
    "Average Speed differences are expected to be smaller in magnitude compared to Success and Time-to-Target, given the smaller SD relative to the mean."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "The 'Success' variable is binary (0/1), making standard ANOVA inappropriate; treating it as continuous ignores the distributional constraints and may yield misleading p-values.",
    "Unequal sample sizes across paradigms (n=3323 to n=48846) may reduce power for underrepresented groups (Bright Visual Only, Sham) and inflate Type I error if variance is not equal (Welch's ANOVA required).",
    "Potential pseudoreplication: Data contains 76,655 rows but only 8 unique Mouse IDs are listed in the top levels; if multiple trials per mouse exist, standard ANOVA violates the independence assumption without random effects.",
    "Extreme outliers in 'Time-to-Target' (max 201.39) and 'Path Efficiency' (max 29.81) could disproportionately influence the F-statistic in standard ANOVA."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a Generalized Linear Mixed Model (GLMM) for 'Success' (Binomial distribution, random intercept for Mouse) and Linear Mixed Models (LMM) for the continuous variables (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with 'Mouse' as a random effect to properly account for repeated measures and non-normal distributions."
}
